newsitem.title: NORWAY: Strong bank shares boost Oslo bourse to life high.
newsitem.headline: Strong bank shares boost Oslo bourse to life high.

text.p: The Norwegian share index rose to a record close on Monday with the banking sector leading the way on a day with moderate trade.
Oslo's Total share index closed at 1,289,13 points, up 0.34 percent from Friday after first soaring to an intra-day all-time high of 1,293.24 at lunchtime. Turnover was 811 million crowns.

"Sentiment is fairly good," one dealer said. "Bank shares are strong because the market is expecting strong profits from the banks this week. I think the shares will continue to perform well, but we may see some profit-taking after the results are out."
Den norske Bank (DnB) jumped 2.48 percent to 33.10 crowns and Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse was up 2.95 percent at 27.90 crowns. Both will present first-half 1997 results on Wednesday.
Union Bank of Norway (UBN) will announce its results on Thursday. Its primary capital certificate, a hybrid share, increased 1.29 percent in value to 235 crowns.
A dealer attributed UBN's rise partly to expectations of profits for unlisted Fellesdata, a software company that is 33 percent owned by the savings bank.
